subject: Canary SLA drift — request for per-route cost attribution + root-cause dashboard
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Canary SLA drift — request for per-route cost attribution + root-cause dashboard

Folks,

Last night's canary rollout for the new routing policy in us-west saw a ~15% SLO violation spike between 01:40–02:15 PT. Support already has a ticket from Acme (INC-4582) and they flagged cost growth on a handful of routes (token spend up ~2.1x).

We need a short-term and mid-term plan to give operators: 
- A per-route cost breakdown (tokens, model variant, quantization) by minute, with the ability to slice by tenant.
- Latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) over the same window side-by-side with cost.
- A "compare to baseline" quick view (last 6h vs rolling 7d median).
- Root-cause signals: model-variant swaps, batch-size shifts, KV cache hit-rate, and any sudden change in prompt length mix.
- An actionable button in the console (rollback to previous route / force-model-variant) or a link to trigger an ops runbook.

Constraints: we want this light-weight — avoid full raw-token retention if possible. Start with derived aggregates plus a sampling path for detailed traces. Ideally a dev-facing incremental UI we can hand to SEs within 2 sprints and a follow-up ops dashboard for engineers.

Can you reply with: owner for telemetry work, a proposed minimal data schema we need (tags/metrics), and rough ETA for an MVP? If we can have a quick prototype by next Wednesday that would help calm Acme.

Attachments: incident-screenshot-1.png (high-level spike), sample-query-log-20280728.csv (filtered queries from affected routes)

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Canary SLA drift — request for per-route cost attribution + root-cause dashboard

Vivek —

Thanks for the context and the attachments. Quick thoughts / clarifying Qs: 

1) Incremental approach I recommend:
   - Phase 1 (short, low infra): per-route aggregated metrics at 1-minute granularity (tokens, duration, p50/p95/p99, cache-hit%). UI: compare last 6h vs 7d median and a compact heatmap.
   - Phase 2: sampled trace extraction (5–10% of calls) that pulls full prompt/response + model-variant and batch info for deep dives.
   - Phase 3: retention-backed analytics and tenant-level cost attribution.

2) Minimal telemetry schema (proposal): 
   - tags: route_id, tenant_id, model_variant, quantization_profile, region, deployment_tag
   - metrics: token_in, token_out, request_duration_ms, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, queued_ms

3) Backend complexity: we currently export per-request metrics to Prometheus + trace IDs to Honeycomb, but we lack a consistent route_id tag in all layers (some legacy paths use endpoint_name). Adding route_id across ingestion, router, and executor is the path of least surprise but will take ~3 dev days with tests.

If we aim for a prototype dashboard driven by aggregated metrics, estimate: 2 devs (metrics + UI) for 10 working days to get Phase 1. If we include sampled trace plumbing for Phase 2, add another 8–10 days.

Owner: I'll take telemetry schema and Phase 1 ingestion changes. Marcus, can you own the UI prototype?

--

Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Canary SLA drift — request for per-route cost attribution + root-cause dashboard

Team,

Acme is the customer who hit support. They are mid-market, on an annual contract, and this deployment is in a P0 evaluation for a bigger renewal next quarter. I spoke to their AE — they reported increased costs and intermittent timeouts in the morning window. Risk: potential pullback of the rollout and a paused renewal discussion.

If Phase 1 prototype can be available to SEs within 2 sprints, that would buy us time. In the short-term, can we give them a readout and the exported sample CSV (the attached sample-query-log-20280728.csv) so their engineering lead can correlate on their side?

Owner/ask to product: we need an explicit customer-facing one-pager that explains what is being collected, retention, and access — SES will share.

-Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick follow-up. We saw the spike in the morning (01:45–02:05 PT) — increased latency and higher token counts for our chat routes. The CSV you shared lines up with what our telemetry shows.

Two asks from Acme engineering: 
- Can you provide a short export we can ingest (minute granularity) so we can run a side-by-side comparison?
- A weekly sync with your engineering lead this week would be helpful to review prototype progress and avoid a step-back on rollout.

Happy to jump on a call tomorrow afternoon PT.

Best,
Jordan Lee
